title: VST image of the star-forming region Messier 17
caption: The Omega Nebula, Messier 17, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope
celestial: M 17, Messier 17 · constellation Sagittarius · about 5500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #15 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This is Messier 17, also called the Omega Nebula or the Swan Nebula, a sprawling region of gas, dust and hot young stars at the heart of our galaxy, in the constellation Sagittarius (the Archer). It was the first image released from the VLT Survey Telescope, or VST.

Star-forming regions like this are where clouds of gas collapse into new stars. The hot young stars that result pour out energy that makes the surrounding gas glow and shapes the clouds they were born from.

The VST was built to survey large patches of sky. Its field of view is wide enough to take in the whole nebula, including its fainter outer parts, while staying sharp from edge to edge. The raw data were turned into this picture with Astro-WISE, software created by E.A. Valentijn with colleagues in Groningen and other institutions.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (53.40 x 53.40 arcminutes) and distance (5500 light years), the frame spans roughly 85 × 85 light-years. Its light set out about 5,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from the OmegaCAM camera on the VLT Survey Telescope, using filters in visible light and the near-infrared. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Part of the data is near-infrared, which the eye cannot see, and long exposures pick up faint outer gas beyond what the eye could detect.

behind.people: See full credit: ESO/INAF-VST/OmegaCAM. Acknowledgement: OmegaCen/Astro-WISE/Kapteyn Institute
behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

alt: A wide view of a large star-forming nebula of gas, dust and young stars.
